label: fed-back "j" early in the copy phase
explanation: Copy-phase token feature for the letter j. It fires when the input is j (the model feeding back its own j output) during the first few copy steps (recall_idx 1-3, absolute step <= 9). Magnitude is highest at recall_idx 1, i.e. right after <DEL> in sequences that start with j (83% of activation mass; the top examples are all j x x x <DEL> [j]), especially in short sequences (L = 4-5). It falls off for j at recall_idx 2-3 and in longer sequences, and is roughly silent for j at later copy positions. It does not fire in the original phase (0.1% of mass), including on original j tokens, or at the delimiter, and is almost never active on other input tokens (h, m, 3, etc. give only tiny activations).

issues: The main claims hold. 98.2% of activation mass is on in_tok == j. The original phase holds 0.1% of the mass and the delimiter 0%. recall_idx 1 holds 83.1%, recall_idx 2 holds 13.9% and recall_idx 3 holds 2.9%. recall_idx >= 4 holds exactly 0 (precision 0 over 41k j steps), so 'mostly inactive' understates it: the feature is fully off there.

The predicate's cutoff (recall_idx <= 3 & t <= 9) produces a systematic class of false positives: 8712 inactive steps on test. The precision grid over (recall_idx, L) for j shows the feature fires when L + 2*recall_idx <= 10 (equivalently t + recall_idx <= 10). Inside that region precision is 0.76-1.0; outside it, it drops sharply.

Grid cells inside the predicate but outside the real boundary: r=2 L=7 (t=9) precision 0.12; r=3 L=5 (t=8) precision 0.27; r=3 L=6 (t=9) precision 0.01. Test misses show these as j fed back at step 8-9 at recall_idx 2-3 in L=5-7 sequences.
Cells the predicate cuts off but that sit near the boundary: r=1 L=9 (t=10) precision 0.14, which is fine to exclude. r=1 L=8 (t=9) is 0.83, which the predicate correctly includes.

Missed activations (2.1% of mass on test) are faint activations (about 0.01-0.07 of max) on non-j tokens. They sit mostly at recall_idx 1 with L=4, spread across many tokens, with precision 0.05 for that cell. This is low-magnitude noise, not a counterexample class.
The original predicate's test F1 is 0.770, below the 0.8 bar. The revised predicate reaches test F1 0.848 (precision 0.936, recall 0.776, mass recall 0.974), with matching dev scores (F1 0.851).
